# Core Concepts & Formulae: Kinematics (v.3)

This list is organized to follow the instructional sequence, moving from basic definitions to the application of equations.

## 1. Fundamental Quantities

- **Position ($$x$$)**: An object's location relative to a reference point (origin). It is a vector quantity.
- **Distance ($$d$$)**: The total length of the path traveled. It is a scalar quantity.
- **Displacement ($$\Delta x$$)**: The change in an object's position. It is a vector quantity, calculated as:
  $$\Delta x = x_1 - x_0$$
  where $$x_1$$ is the final position and $$x_0$$ is the initial position.
- **Speed**: The rate at which an object covers distance. It is a scalar quantity.
- **Velocity ($$v$$)**: The rate of change of an object's position. It is a vector quantity.
- **Average Velocity ($$\bar{v}$$)**:
  $$\bar{v} = \frac{\Delta x}{\Delta t} = \frac{x_1 - x_0}{t_1 - t_0}$$
- **Acceleration ($$a$$)**: The rate of change of an object's velocity. It is a vector quantity.
- **Average Acceleration ($$\bar{a}$$)**:
  $$\bar{a} = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} = \frac{v_1 - v_0}{t_1 - t_0}$$

## 2. Graphical Analysis of Motion

### Position vs. Time Graph ($$x$$-$$t$$)
- The slope of the line represents velocity.
- A straight line indicates constant velocity.
- A curved line indicates changing velocity (acceleration).

### Velocity vs. Time Graph ($$v$$-$$t$$)
- The slope of the line represents acceleration.
- The area under the curve represents displacement ($$\Delta x$$).

### Acceleration vs. Time Graph ($$a$$-$$t$$)
- The area under the curve represents the change in velocity ($$\Delta v$$).

## 3. Kinematic Equations (for Constant Acceleration)

These equations describe the motion of an object when its acceleration is uniform.

### Velocity-Time Relation:
$$v_1 = v_0 + at$$

### Position-Time Relation:
$$\Delta x = v_0t + \frac{1}{2}at^2$$

### Velocity-Position Relation:
$$v_1^2 = v_0^2 + 2a\Delta x$$

## 4. Special Case: Freefall

Freefall is the motion of an object under the influence of gravity alone, with air resistance considered negligible.
The acceleration is constant and directed downwards.

### Acceleration due to Gravity ($$a_g$$):
$$a = a_g \approx -9.80 \, \text{m}/\text{s}^2$$
(The negative sign indicates a downward direction).
